summary: 100-foot wooden lookout built 1935 in Seattle's Cedar River watershed, King County, WA; gone after 1969, though sources disagree on destroyed versus removed; permission needed.

facts.design: 7x7 wooden cab with catwalk on a 100-foot wooden tower with a ground house (the register calls the cab an L-6 wooden cab)
facts.status_note: Destroyed in 1969 per firelookout.com and Willhite; the register says removed in 1969; a 1975 USGS map caption on the Willhite page shows a lookout on Little Mountain.

access.note: Willhite: permission or a guide needed from City of Seattle Watershed

visit.trail_note: Willhite lists 0.4 miles and 220 feet of elevation gain; permission or a guide is required.

events.note: Materials sent to the summit by logging skyline cable so no road was needed; 100-foot wooden tower with a 7x7 cab
Site considered for an Aircraft Warning Service post; tower judged too high for continuous winter use
Register says the cab and ground house were removed
USGS map caption on the Willhite page shows a lookout on Little Mountain; this conflicts with a 1969 end

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Firelookout.com and Willhite say destroyed in 1969; the register says the cab and ground house were removed in 1969. The year agrees, and the story reports both words. A 1975 USGS map caption on the Willhite page shows a lookout, which the sources do not explain; this is left unresolved.
The register calls the cab an L-6 wooden cab; firelookout.com and Willhite describe a 7x7 wooden cab. The story gives both.

notes_for_editor: Construction details come from Willhite quoting a July 1935 article (Six Twenty-Six); I did not verify the article itself. A Seattle archive result from a search summary (1954 photos) was not confirmed; the archive pages returned a CAPTCHA, so it is left out. The 1975 USGS caption conflicts with the 1969 end and is unresolved. The 'Distance' figure is from Willhite and its start point is not stated.
